transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-15 15:00 PDT | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (CTO - Atlas), Dana Ruiz (ML Eng), Oliver Grant (Head of Infra), Sofia Park (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick POC scoping to align on benchmark plan, harness integration, what scripts Atlas will run, and timeline for a 3-week pilot. Discussed streaming vs non-streaming requirements and success criteria (p95 latency, throughput targets, cost per 1M tokens).

00:00 Jordan Lee: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll get started — Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. voicing connection ok?
00:12 Marcus Chen: Yeah good here, thanks Jordan. Dana and Oliver are on from our side.
00:17 Jordan Lee: Great, quick agenda — scoping the POC, agree success criteria, talk harness + scripts, and timeline. Priya will cover the perf and streaming details.
00:29 Priya Nair: Hi all, yeah I'll go through the benchmark harness integration options and what we usually ask for from customers. A couple caveats up front, transcription might have some typos in names in our notes.
00:40 Dana Ruiz: Cool. Our main ask — we need to validate latency at p95 and cost per 100k requests for our chat assistant. We're concerned about streaming since we do token-by-token UI and want sub-300ms chunk delivery.
00:55 Priya Nair: Okay good — so two axes: non-streaming throughput/latency per complete response and streaming token delivery latency. For non-streaming we measure end-to-end p50/p95 and server-side tokens/sec, for streaming we instrument time-to-first-token and chunk interval.
01:15 Marcus Chen: Can you explain the harness? We have some existing JMeter and locust scripts but not model-aware harnesses.
01:24 Samir Patel: Sure — Redwood's benchmark harness is a small repo with examples. We can run in two modes: customer-run (you run harness against Redwood endpoints with your traces) or Redwood-run (we run tests in our infra on a dedicated test queue). The repo includes sample scripts in Python + Locust and a streaming client that mimics chunked outputs.
01:44 Dana Ruiz: Do you have example payload shapes? We have multi-turn context, system prompts, and attachments (metadata).
01:52 Priya Nair: Yes. We'll ask you to share 3 canonical prompt flows and request traces. We recommend anonymizing PHI but keeping shape and sizes. For attachment metadata we simulate 2-5KB additional context per turn.
02:10 Oliver Grant: On the infra side — we need to know if the POC needs VPC peering or just API keys. Also KMS for key management?
02:20 Jordan Lee: For pilot we usually start with API-key access to hosted endpoints; if data residency/VPC is required we can do Dedicated or Private. We'll capture your KMS/SSO requirements in the security doc.
02:33 Marcus Chen: Success criteria — we want p95 latency < 800ms for non-streaming responses under 10 RPS sustained, and streaming time-to-first-token < 250ms with token-to-token under 100ms at 3 concurrent sessions. Price per 1M tokens target below $15 to be competitive.
02:54 Priya Nair: Those are reasonable guardrails; we'll translate into concrete tests: baseline non-streaming at 10 RPS with your average payload size (you'll provide), ramp to 50 RPS for stress, and streaming tests with realistic chunk sizes.
03:11 Dana Ruiz: What's the recommended concurrency? Our current peak is ~150 concurrent users, but average is 20.
03:18 Priya Nair: For the POC we typically size tests around average and peak: run average-profile test at 20 concurrent, peak stress at 150. Also measure cold-start vs steady state — we instrument warm cache vs cold.
03:33 Marcus Chen: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? We rely on a little bit of reuse in conversation.
03:40 Samir Patel: The harness can replay prefixes to measure cache hit effects. We'll provide toggles for full-cache, partial-prefix, and no-cache to show delta on tokens/sec and latency.
03:52 Sofia Park: For product we'll be interested in variance — p95 vs p99 and tail latencies. If p99 is bad we might need to reconsider.
04:02 Priya Nair: We'll capture p50/p90/p95/p99 and mean tokens/sec, and we'll provide plots. Also a cost model estimate from Redwood Optimize to show cost per request at configured batching/quantization.
04:17 Marcus Chen: Security checklist — we require SOC2, SAML SSO for our team, audit logs, and control plane isolation. Also need to know about log retention and whether user prompt text is persisted.
04:30 Jordan Lee: We have SOC 2, SSO/SAML and can provide audit log examples. For hosted POC prompts are logged for debugging but can be disabled; we also have encryption at rest with optional customer KMS for Private setups. We'll send our security pack.
04:46 Dana Ruiz: For harness integration — how do we feed our traces? Can the harness accept gzipped ndjson event traces?
04:53 Samir Patel: Yes, the harness accepts ndjson with schema in the README, and we have a small converter script. We can also accept CSVs. We'll add an example for multi-turn traces.
05:05 Marcus Chen: Streaming: is the client-side SDK required? We have a React/TypeScript UI using SSE currently.
05:12 Priya Nair: We have a streaming SDK in JS that supports SSE and Websocket; the harness has a streaming client that mimics your SSE chunking pattern to measure chunk latency and reassembly overhead.
05:25 Oliver Grant: Any dependency on GPU type for benchmarking? We have internal preferences for A100 vs H100.
05:32 Priya Nair: The benchmark will report model variant for each run; if you want us to run on Dedicated with H100 we can schedule that but usually we run on our curated open-model variants with GPU profile metadata. If hardware matters to you we'll note it as part of test matrix.
05:50 Dana Ruiz: We also care about quantized vs fp16 accuracy/regression. Can the harness run evals to check output quality when we change quantization?
05:58 Samir Patel: Yes we can plug in an eval set and run quality checks — BLEU/ROUGE or custom fidelity metrics on your prompts. We'll surface any regressions as part of the POC report.
06:12 Marcus Chen: Timeline? We want a 3-week POC starting next Monday ideally.
06:17 Jordan Lee: Timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) agree scoping and collect traces; week 1 baseline non-streaming tests + streaming integration; week 2 stress tests, quantization variants, and evals; week 3 recap + detailed report with cost estimates. If starting Monday 2026-06-22 we can deliver final report by 2026-07-13.
06:36 Dana Ruiz: Sounds good. Any blockers for us to share traces? PHI scrub is required, we'll anonymize but maintain structure.
06:45 Priya Nair: That's fine — please follow the sample anonymization script we include. Also please flag any payloads with PII.
06:55 Marcus Chen: What are the main risk factors? I'm thinking integration time and streaming fragility.
07:02 Samir Patel: Integration risks: getting exact trace shape, network egress for streaming tests, and if you request Dedicated hardware that scheduling may add lead time. We'll note mitigation steps: we run a Redwood-hosted baseline while you run local harness to parallelize.
07:19 Sofia Park: On success criteria — can you put a pass/fail matrix in the final deck? e.g., p95 < 800ms pass, between 800-1.2s caution, >1.2s fail.
07:27 Priya Nair: Yes, we'll include a matrix and recommended remediation (batching, cache tuning, quantization).
07:36 Marcus Chen: Any concerns about regulatory/compliance while sending traces? We'll use anonymized traces but need an NDA addendum maybe.
07:44 Jordan Lee: We can route that through legal. I'll include a note to our CSM to surface the NDA addendum and security pack.
07:53 Dana Ruiz: For the harness scripts — can you provide a sample locustfile and a streaming client example?
07:58 Samir Patel: Absolutely, we'll attach sample locustfiles and a JS streaming client. The repo also has a docker-compose to run locally.
08:08 Marcus Chen: Metrics we'd expect in the final report: p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, failed-request rate, and streaming chunk latency distribution.
08:21 Priya Nair: We'll include all those, plus regression checks for quality metrics, and a per-model variant summary.
08:29 Jordan Lee: Recap of next steps: Jordan to send harness link + security pack; Dana to share traces and prompts; Priya to schedule streaming deep-dive and prepare demo scripts; Oliver to confirm network/KMS details.
08:44 Marcus Chen: Good, thanks. Any final Qs?
08:48 Oliver Grant: No, we'll start prepping traces.
08:51 Jordan Lee: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the links and next meeting invite.
08:57 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker overlap, some names mis-typed.

References mentioned: benchmark harness repo (link to be shared), sample locustfiles, Redwood security pack (link), streaming SDK (JS example).

POC success criteria (as captured):
- Performance: non-streaming p95 < 800ms at 10 RPS baseline; stress ramp to 50 RPS; p99 target to be evaluated.
- Streaming: time-to-first-token < 250ms; token-token interval < 100ms for interactive feel.
- Quality: no regressions >5% on customer-supplied evals when testing quantized variants.
- Cost: estimate cost per 1M tokens < $15 for baseline config.

Benchmark plan summary:
- Data needed: 3 canonical prompt flows, 2 weeks of request traces (ndjson), typical payload sizes, concurrency profile.
- Tests: baseline non-streaming, streaming token-latency replay, cache hit/miss profiles, stress tests to peak concurrency, quantization variant runs, quality/eval runs.
- Deliverables: raw metrics + plots, pass/fail matrix, cost estimate, remediation suggestions.

End of file.
